Subject: RE: MSA draft -- questions on liability / prepaid credits

Hi Irene / Karthik,

Thanks for sending the latest MSA. We reviewed the redline and have two substantive asks before we can move to procurement:

1) The limitation of liability section currently caps damages at the aggregate fees paid in the prior 12 months. ACME has material prepaid items (annual committed spend). We need clarity on whether that cap would apply to: (a) termination for convenience (prepaid credits for unused months), and (b) any wind-down assistance charges we incur to transition away.

2) We also want carve-outs for consequences arising from security incidents and IP infringement claims. The current LoL language seems to limit those in a way that would leave ACME with little remedy.

Attached is our annotated redline (ACME_MSA_redline_from_client.docx). Can Redwood confirm (i) what you will treat as an LoL carve-out (e.g., willful misconduct, gross negligence, breaches of confidentiality, IP infringement, security/breach obligations), and (ii) whether prepaid/unused fees will be refunded/credited on termination or only converted to service credits?

Our procurement team is on a tight schedule and would like a short call if you prefer to discuss live.

Best,
Emily Stone
General Counsel
ACME Corp

Emily —

Appreciate the clear redline. Quick summary of Redwood’s position so you can share with your procurement team:

- LoL carve-outs: Redwood cannot accept an LoL that eliminates remedies for (i) Redwood’s indemnity obligations for third-party IP claims, (ii) obligations arising from Redwood’s willful misconduct or gross negligence, or (iii) violations of confidentiality/security obligations. We are comfortable adding explicit carve-outs for those categories so they are not swept into the general cap.

- Prepaid fees / termination: For termination for convenience, Redwood’s standard is to offer a prorated credit for unused prepaid months OR a refund in cases where an enterprise has an administrative need (e.g., procurement rules) — we can be flexible subject to deal economics. For termination for cause related to Redwood’s breach, we typically provide a refund/credit of unused prepaid fees prorated to the effective termination date.

- Wind-down assistance: Redwood can commit to a reasonable amount of wind-down assistance (knowledge transfer, export of KV cache, short-term rehosting support) as a professional services engagement. We can include a limited commitment in the MSA: up to 90 days of transition support or a capped amount of professional services (whichever is smaller). We generally do not allow wind-down assistance to expand the LoL or create additional open-ended exposure.

I’m looping in Lauren (legal lead) and Karhik (AE) on options we can propose in redline form. To move this forward quickly, our suggested compromise is: a LoL cap equal to the greater of (i) fees paid in prior 12 months OR (ii) $250,000, with explicit carve-outs for: willful misconduct, gross negligence, breach of confidentiality/security obligations (including data breach liability), and indemnities for IP infringement. For prepaid fees/termination, propose explicit language: prorated refund of unused prepaid fees on termination for cause; for convenience termination, prorated credits unless procurement requires a cash refund (in which case we agree to refund, subject to a maximum equal to 6 months of prepaid fees).

We’ll attach a proposed redline with the exact contract language. If that approach is acceptable, we can provide final MSA text and a short one-page matrix showing exposures.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Director, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Team / Emily —

Below is language we can offer in the MSA to balance ACME’s concerns with Redwood’s need to limit open-ended risk. This text is intended to be inserted into the LoL and the termination sections; minimal tweaks can make it fit your form.

1) Limitation of Liability (carve-outs):
Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the limitations of liability set forth in this Section shall not apply to: (a) either party’s indemnification obligations for third-party claims of intellectual property infringement; (b) damages arising from a party’s willful misconduct or gross negligence; (c) a party’s breach of its confidentiality or data security obligations (including obligations under the Data Processing Addendum); and (d) amounts payable under Section [Indemnities].

2) Cap calculation:
Except for the carve-outs above, each party’s aggregate liability for direct damages arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be limited to the greater of (i) fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the Order Form(s) for the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to liability; or (ii) $250,000.

3) Prepaid fees and termination credits:
If Customer terminates the Order Form for cause due to a material, uncured breach by Redwood, Customer shall be entitled to a prorated refund of any prepaid, unused fees for the remainder of the applicable prepaid period. If Customer terminates for convenience, Customer shall be entitled to a prorated credit for unused prepaid fees unless Customer’s procurement rules require a cash refund, in which case Redwood will provide a cash refund limited to six (6) months of prepaid fees. Any refund or credit shall be reduced by any non-refundable onboarding or professional services fees specifically identified in the Order Form.

4) Wind-down assistance:
Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide transition assistance for up to ninety (90) days after termination at no additional charge in circumstances where Redwood is the terminating party’s primary inference provider and the termination is not caused by Customer’s breach; provided, however, that Redwood’s aggregate liability for transition assistance under this Section shall be limited to the lesser of (a) 90 days of assistance as described herein or (b) $100,000 in fees. Additional transition support beyond this scope shall be available at Redwood’s then-current professional services rates.

Lauren — happy to adjust dollar caps/periods based on ACME scale. If ACME pushes back on the cap floor ($250k) we can propose a sliding scale tied to committed ARR.

-Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
